title: Most Frequent IDs
summary: Given two arrays, nums and freq of equal length n, where nums[i] is an ID and freq[i] indicates the number of times to add or remove that ID at step i.
statement: Given two arrays, nums and freq of equal length n, where nums[i] is an ID and freq[i] indicates the number of times to add or remove that ID at step i. Track the frequency of the most frequent ID after each step. If the collection is empty at any step, the count is 0.
constraints: nums and freq have equal positive length; each step adds freq[i] to that ID count.
Updates never make an ID count negative, and a zero count represents absence.
Return the greatest current count after each update, or zero when every count is zero.
known_wrong_solutions:
def most_frequent_id_counts(nums,freq):
    from heapq import heappop,heappush
    counts={};heap=[];answer=[]
    for identifier,change in zip(nums,freq):
        counts[identifier]=counts.get(identifier,0)+change
        heappush(heap,(-counts[identifier],identifier))

        answer.append(-heap[0][0] if heap else 0)
    return answer
def most_frequent_id_counts(nums,freq):
    from heapq import heappop,heappush
    counts={};heap=[];answer=[]
    for identifier,change in zip(nums,freq):
        counts[identifier]=counts.get(identifier,0)+max(change,0)
        heappush(heap,(-counts[identifier],identifier))
        while heap and -heap[0][0]!=counts[heap[0][1]]:heappop(heap)
        answer.append(-heap[0][0] if heap else 0)
    return answer
hints: Each update invalidates the prior heap entry for one ID, but removing arbitrary heap entries eagerly is unnecessary.
Push every new count and lazily pop while the heap top disagrees with the authoritative count map.
Update count[id], push (-count,id), discard stale tops, and append the current top count.
The map is authoritative; after stale tops are removed, no valid count exceeds the maximum-heap top, so it is exactly the current maximum.
